notes:
Top-line: SMB helpdesk SaaS building an in-app chat and automated ticket summarization feature. Trialing Redwood hosted API — self-serve devs onboarded with test key. Primary concerns: pick a model that hits conversational quality while keeping token spend under control. They asked about Llama vs Mistral vs Qwen variants and cost/latency tradeoffs.

Details / quotes: 
- 'We need a model that sounds natural in short support replies but we can't spend on largest Llama variants.'
- POC scope: agent-facing assistant + nightly batch ticket summarization for 500–1,500 tickets/day. Expected concurrency 10–50 rps at peak, typical session length 20–120 tokens. Latency target ~<200ms for single-turn chat, willing to accept up to 500ms for longer summarization jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: target <$0.01 per user session on average; total monthly token budget estimated ~$3k-$8k during pilot.

Model questions raised by SE call (Leo):
- Which Mistral/Qwen/Llama flavors are in hosted catalog and which hit the lowest cost point for similar quality?
- Any recommended quantized variants for chat to reduce cost without big loss in instruction-following for short replies?
- Can Redwood provide sample per-token latency and cost for 13B vs 7B vs distilled variants on our typical sequence lengths?
- How does auto-routing/fallback work if a chosen variant is overloaded — will it switch to cheaper/less capable variant transparently?

Security / compliance: SOC2 is required for vendor selection; SSO via SAML necessary for product team access; want audit logs of request-level activity during evaluation. Public cloud only; no VPC/on-prem now.

Next-step notes: Prepare a concise one-page model comparison (13B vs 7B vs distilled) showing expected latency, typical perplexity/quality signals for short replies, and cost per 1k tokens under Redwood hosted pricing. Include recommended defaults for chat (low-latency) and nightly batch summarization (cost-optimized). Schedule CTO + product engineer 30m Q&A next week.
